name: Weft
author: E. T. Carter
description: A woven cloth seen close. Bright vertical warp threads and horizontal weft threads interlace in a plain tabby weave — at every crossing one rides over and the other dips under, in the checkerboard the loom makes. A soft sheen sweeps diagonally so the raised threads glint as light crosses the cloth, threads tinted by position, the whole weave breathing with a slow ripple. A direct sibling of warp, where the weft is now real interlaced thread.

params.label: Thread spacing
params.effect: Distance between threads in CSS px; dense fine cloth at the minimum, open coarse weave at the maximum.

params.label: Thread width
params.effect: Half-width of each thread in CSS px with its halo scaling alongside; fine yarn to thick glowing cord.

params.label: Ripple
params.effect: Amplitude of the slow cloth ripple; 0 holds a taut flat weave, high lets the fabric billow and breathe.

params.label: Sheen
params.effect: Strength of the diagonal light sweep catching the raised threads; 0 is a matte weave, high a bright satin glint.

params.label: Sheen speed
params.effect: Speed the sheen band travels across the cloth; 0 holds it still, high sweeps the light briskly across.

params.label: Glow
params.effect: Overall thread emission; low is a quiet cloth, high a luminous woven sheet.

params.label: Relief
params.effect: How deeply the under-thread dips at each crossing; 0 flattens the weave into a plain grid, high makes the over-under interlace read as real raised cloth.
